case_title: Meera v. State by the Inspector of Police Thiruvotriyur Police Station Chennai
mitigating_circumstances: Incident occurred in 2006, appellant is approximately 80 years old
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 498A IPC, sentenced to one year R.I. and fine of Rs.1,000/-
high_court_outcome: Partly allowed the appeal, acquitted accused for Section 306 IPC, maintained conviction for Section 498A IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the mother-in-law of the deceased, was alleged to have subjected the deceased to torture and cruelty regarding jewels. The deceased was staying with her in-laws while her husband was abroad. The prosecution presented evidence from multiple witnesses, including the mother and father of the deceased, who testified about the harassment. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 498A IPC and sentenced her to one year of rigorous imprisonment with a fine. The High Court upheld the conviction but reduced the sentence to three months of rigorous imprisonment with the same fine. The Supreme Court confirmed the conviction and reduced the sentence further to three months of rigorous imprisonment.
